talkshows.title: TVRI Talk Show: Network Topology Design & Resilient Infrastructure

talkshows.title: TVRI Talk Show: High-Speed Network Architectures for Big Data

talkshows.title: TVRI Talk Show: Computer Network Performance Modeling & Simulation

keynotes.title: Guest Lecture at Sunway University
keynotes.event: Designing for Every Screen: Responsive Interfaces for Digital Literacy
keynotes.abstract:
On the morning of 26 November 2026 (8:00–9:45 AM MYT), I had the privilege and honor of being invited as a Guest Lecturer at Sunway University (Faculty of Arts & Social Sciences) for Week 8 of the Digital Media Literacy (COM2023 – COM2024) course in Uni Lecture Theatre 6.

What made this morning truly unforgettable was the remarkable diversity in the room. I had the joy of sharing ideas and learning alongside international students from the United Kingdom, Turkmenistan, Pakistan, Japan, China, and South Korea, together with their Malaysian peers. Teaching interface design in such a multicultural setting is always energizing: every student brings a different set of digital habits, favorite apps, and cultural perspectives on how people read and interact on screens.

opinions.title: The Metaverse in Higher Education: Smart Campus Development at UBD’s PKKMB
opinions.abstract: At the 2022 New Student Orientation (PKKMB) of the Faculty of Computer Science, Universitas Bina Darma (UBD), incoming students were introduced to the potential of metaverse technologies in higher education. Faculty Dean Dr. Tata Sutabri highlighted the convergence of Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) as pivotal catalysts for building a futuristic Smart Campus. The orientation attended by academic leadership including Head of Information Systems Dr. Zaid Amin and Head of Informatics Alek Wijaya emphasized equipping students with early digital literacy to embrace virtual learning, collaborative simulation, and future-ready IT infrastructure.

opinions.title: 2024 ICIBA-SOSIEC Chair and Universiti Malaya Bolster International Partnership
opinions.abstract: In November 2024, Universitas Bina Darma (UBD), Indonesia, formally established an international academic partnership with Universiti Malaya (UM), Malaysia, through the execution of an Implementation Arrangement (IA) at the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, Universiti Malaya. Represented by the 2024 ICIBA-SOSIEC Conference Chair, Zaid Amin, M.Kom., Ph.D., alongside Universiti Malaya’s Gender Studies Programme Coordinator and Keynote Speaker, Dr. Ruhana binti Padzil, the agreement institutionalizes bilateral collaboration anchored in the annual International Conference on Information Technology and Business Applications (ICIBA) and the International Conference on Social Sciences, Humanities, and Economics (SOSIEC). The partnership establishes a strategic framework for joint cross-border research, co-authored monographs, international journal publications, and high-level scholarly exchange, with select conference findings curated in international proceedings. Partnering with Universiti Malaya ranked 60th globally in the 2025 QS World University Rankings and 3rd in Southeast Asia, demonstrates UBD’s institutional commitment to fostering high-impact global research networks and advancing cross-disciplinary academic excellence across technology, media, and social sciences.

opinions.title: New Scholarly Book by Dr. Zaid Amin Explores the Mechanics of AI-Driven Digital Habits
opinions.abstract: In his latest book, Persuasive Technology: AI for Shaping Behavior and Habits, Dr. Zaid Amin investigates how artificial intelligence has evolved into an active force shaping everyday digital behaviors. Synthesizing insights from computing, psychology, and ethics, the book demystifies how corporations and digital platforms utilize predictive algorithms to guide consumer choices, while addressing the critical ethical boundaries surrounding digital addiction and cognitive manipulation. Serving as both a scholarly reference and a practical guide, the book provides actionable strategies for designing ethical, transparent, and user-empowering AI technologies in the modern digital age.

opinions.title: Dr. Zaid Amin’s Team Awarded 2025 Kemendikbudristek Community Service Grant
opinions.abstract: Traditional household-level agricultural micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) often face significant operational bottlenecks, including volatile crop yields, labor-intensive cultivation, and restricted market penetration. This community service project, funded under the 2025 Batch III Community Service (PkM) Grant by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology (Kemendikbudristek) Indonesia, introduces an integrated socio-technical framework to empower the instant ginger home industry at UPPKA Kampung KB Layang-Layang in Palembang. Led by a multidisciplinary team from Universitas Bina Darma and Universitas Muhammadiyah Palembang, the intervention operationalizes two complementary technological pillars: (1) an Internet of Things (IoT)-based Smart Farming system deploying real-time soil moisture and ambient temperature sensors to optimize irrigation efficiency, mitigate climate vulnerability, and ensure consistent rhizome yields; and (2) an attention-driven Persuasive Technology and Digital Branding model that equips local producers with modern packaging design, emotional brand storytelling, and multi-channel digital marketing capabilities across e-commerce and social platforms. By actively involving local homemakers and youth in hygienic production and digital literacy workshops, the initiative transitions traditional artisanal processing into a sustainable, resilient, and market-ready agro-business. This model provides an actionable blueprint for university-community partnerships leveraging applied computing to drive grassroots socioeconomic empowerment.

opinions.title: Dr. Zaid Amin (UBD), Prof. Alan F. Smeaton (DCU), and Assoc. Prof. Nazlena Mohamad Ali (UKM) Launch Landmark Book on Information Sharing
opinions.abstract:
"Information Sharing Behaviour on Social Media"

Authors: Zaid Amin, Nazlena Mohamad Ali, & Alan F. Smeaton (Penerbit UKM)

Addressing the escalating challenge of digital misinformation, this international monograph explores the cognitive determinants of user attention in online information-sharing ecosystems. Grounded in a cross-continental collaboration between Universitas Bina Darma (Indonesia), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (Malaysia), and Dublin City University (Ireland), the book introduces the Tune-Attention Model (TAM) and the Visual Selective Attention System (VSAS). It provides researchers and UX architects with actionable, attention-based interaction design principles to mitigate fake news dissemination and foster attentive, responsible digital citizenship.

opinions.title: Dr. Zaid Amin, Informatics Engineering Lecturer at Bina Darma University, appointed External Examiner at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
opinions.abstract:
UBD Informatics Lecturer Dr. Zaid Amin Serves as External PhD Examiner at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia

PALEMBANG — In an active demonstration of cross-border academic collaboration, Zaid Amin, M.Kom., Ph.D., a faculty member in Informatics Engineering at Universitas Bina Darma (UBD) Palembang, was appointed as an External Examiner at the Institute of Visual Informatics (IVI), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM).

Dr. Zaid Amin served on the examination panel for the Doctoral (Ph.D.) Proposal Defense of candidate Anis Juanita Binti Mohd Zainudin (supervised by Senior Research Fellow Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nazlena Mohamad Ali). The doctoral research, titled "A Sharing Behaviour Model Based on Information Characteristics as Misinformation Intervention Strategy," was evaluated virtually via Webex under UKM’s rigorous academic standards.

This international appointment marks a concrete milestone in executing the institutional Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between UBD and UKM. UBD Rector commended the achievement, affirming that it validates the global standing and tangible academic contributions of Universitas Bina Darma on the international stage.

opinions.title: Global Academic Recognition: UBD Palembang Lecturer Appointed as Q1 Journal Reviewer
opinions.abstract:
From Palembang to the Global Stage: UBD Academic Appointed to Prestigious Q1 Journal Review Board

In the global academic arena, peer review is often considered the silent bedrock of scientific progress, a responsibility entrusted only to scholars who have demonstrated rigorous expertise and an uncompromising eye for methodological excellence. For Universitas Bina Darma (UBD) Palembang, that recognition arrived on an international scale when London-based publisher Taylor & Francis Group officially appointed Zaid Amin, M.Kom., Ph.D., as a peer reviewer for the prestigious International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction.

Serving on the review board of a journal with a Scopus Q1 rating, an Impact Factor of 4.7, and a CiteScore of 8.8 is no small feat. It places Dr. Zaid Amin directly at the frontier of human-computer interaction, tasking him with evaluating, critiquing, and shaping research manuscripts submitted by scholars from around the world. Reflecting on the invitation, Dr. Zaid Amin shared his gratitude for seeing his scholarly dedication acknowledged by the worldwide scientific community, noting that being personally sought out by Taylor & Francis was both an honor and a call to maintain the highest standards of academic integrity.

The milestone has drawn warm praise from UBD’s leadership. The Director of the UBD Graduate Program, Prof. Hj. Isnawijayani, M.Si., Ph.D., lauded the appointment as a well-earned testament to Dr. Zaid Amin’s prolific international track record. More than a personal triumph, she highlighted that having faculty members actively shaping premier global literature directly fuels Universitas Bina Darma’s overarching mission: cementing its position as an internationally recognized, technology-driven academic institution on the world stage.

opinions.title: Dr. Zaid Amin receiving the Anugerah Universiti from UKM Chancellor Tuanku Muhriz.
opinions.abstract: Zaid Amin, M.Kom., Ph.D., a lecturer and Head of the Undergraduate Information Systems Program at Universitas Bina Darma (UBD), received the prestigious Anugerah Universiti award from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM). Honored for completing his PhD as a Graduate on Time (GOT) recipient and earning the Best Thesis (Thesis Cemerlang) distinction. Presented directly by UKM Chancellor and Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir, during UKM's 50th Golden Jubilee (Jubli Emas) convocation ceremony on November 26, 2022.

opinions.title: Dr. Zaid Amin of UBD Clinches Best Presenter at IEEE International Conference
opinions.abstract:
At the 4th International Conference on Electronic and Electrical Engineering and Intelligent System (ICE3IS 2024), hosted by Universitas Muhammadiyah Yogyakarta, scholars and industry leaders gathered to address the future of intelligent technologies for sustainable societies. Amidst competitive global presentations, Dr. Zaid Amin, Informatics Engineering Lecturer at Universitas Bina Darma (UBD), distinguished himself on the international stage by clinching the Best Presenter Award.

Dr. Zaid delivered an engaging presentation on his research titled “Tune-Attention Model: Designing Cybernetics Intervention for Information Sharing Behavior,” a collaborative study conducted alongside Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nazlena Mohamad Ali from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM). His paper tackled the pressing digital challenge of cognitive attention and behavioral interventions in online information ecosystems.

The presentation captivated both plenary and technical session audiences, earning top honors at the conference. With the proceedings bound for publication in IEEE Xplore and indexed by Scopus, the achievement underscores UBD’s institutional commitment to fostering internationally benchmarked computational research and cross-border academic excellence.

opinions.title: Moral Decadence and Mental Health in the Era of Society 5.0
opinions.abstract: An op-ed examining the unseen perils of Society 5.0, where rapid advancements in AI and IoT collide with digital addiction, moral decay, and rising mental health challenges among youth. It underscores the urgent need for ethical literacy, self-regulation, and character education to ensure technology serves humanity rather than compromises its core values.

opinions.title: Social Inequality and the Pain of Social Comparison on Social Media
opinions.abstract: An incisive op-ed exploring how social media acts as a magnifying glass for modern inequality. Examining the global phenomenon of public officials flaunting opulent lifestyles ("flexing"), from Indonesia to Nepal, the article highlights how ostentatious displays of wealth not only spark anti-corruption investigations and public outrage, but also inflict deep psychological wounds of social comparison on citizens facing economic hardship.

opinions.title: Polarization in the Digital Age: A Silent Threat to Unity and Democracy
opinions.abstract: An insightful op-ed examining how digital echo chambers and algorithmic curation silently drive societal polarization. Drawing on theories of social capital and digital media dynamics, the article warns that when citizens are divided by online ideological warfare, their collective power to hold authorities accountable weakens—diverting public attention away from critical issues like corruption and socio-economic inequality.
